first_impression.reaction: My assistant shortlisted it because the family wants the legal part done in Sydney and the celebration somewhere else, and we live in Dubai. The first screen is calm and to the point: what it is, the one month to 18 month window, and a line saying it doesn't apply if we marry legally abroad. No gushing. Her summary for me was three lines: lodge it with a Sydney celebrant inside the window, sign it in person in Dubai in front of an authorised witness who isn't a celebrant, and the party abroad is separate. I read the two routes and the close myself. The form steps and document lists are hers.

journey.quote: If you plan to marry legally in another country instead, the NOIM does not come into it: you follow that country's rules.
journey.reaction: Good. It tells me in the second paragraph whether this page is even for us. That respects my time.

journey.section: When do you need to lodge your NOIM?
journey.quote: Treat that as a floor, not a target.
journey.reaction: Short and sensible. With our diaries, nothing happens in a month anyway, so I like that they don't pretend it does.

journey.section: How to fill out the NOIM form step by step
journey.quote: The form was last updated on 1 September 2021.
journey.reaction: Fine for my assistant. The whole step by step part is administration; I skipped it once she said it was straightforward.

journey.quote: If you are outside Australia, your authorised witness must also be outside Australia, and cannot be a celebrant.
journey.reaction: This is the one fact that actually changes something for us, and it is stated plainly. It saved my assistant a phone call.

journey.quote: Plan for an in-person appointment with an authorised witness where you live.
journey.reaction: In Dubai, who is that, and who else sees our passports and personal details at that appointment? The page sends me to the form. I'd rather someone just arranged it quietly.

journey.quote: Keep the originals together in one folder.
journey.reaction: Practical, but it is the family office's job, not mine. Not a reason to stay or leave.

journey.section: Option A: marry legally in Australia, celebrate abroad
journey.quote: You hold a small legal ceremony in Australia with an authorised celebrant, and the NOIM applies exactly as above.
journey.reaction: That is us. A small legal moment in Sydney with close family, then the real wedding elsewhere. Nice to see it described as a normal route, not a workaround.

journey.section: Option A: marry legally in Australia, celebrate abroad
journey.quote: The celebration abroad can then be whatever you want it to be.
journey.reaction: That's the sentence I wanted. Though 'whatever you want' at 300 guests means closed properties and security, and nothing on the page says they've done that.

journey.section: Option A: marry legally in Australia, celebrate abroad
journey.quote: In the Greek Orthodox Archdiocese of Australia, for example, every priest is also a registered civil celebrant, and the NOIM is completed in the priest's presence at least one calendar month before the wedding.
journey.reaction: Shows they think about religious ceremonies, which matters in families like mine. One example only, so I'd still ask how they handle our own customs.

journey.quote: Ask the destination's embassy or consulate whether you need a CNI, where to get it, and whether it needs an authentication or apostille.
journey.reaction: Clear, but it is a lot of 'ask someone else'. My assistant flagged this section as the long one. We're on route A, so I didn't read it.

journey.section: NOIM or marrying abroad: which paperwork applies?
journey.quote: Either way, the legal steps stay with you and your celebrant or the local authority. The celebration is where we come in.
journey.reaction: Understated and honest about where their job starts. I respect a firm that doesn't claim the law.

journey.section: NOIM or marrying abroad: which paperwork applies?
journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor is a single point of contact who plans the venue, travel, vendors and payments for the celebration abroad, works in your time zone and quotes in AUD, with the fee agreed in writing before any work begins; [talk to Wedded Concierge](https://weddedwonderland.com/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=notice-of-intended-marriage&utm_content=secondary) about your plans.
journey.reaction: Sensible, but it is written for someone worried about being overcharged. I'm worried about scale and leaks, and neither is mentioned. One advisor for 300 guests across three countries? I'd want to hear who else is behind them.

journey.quote: Once the NOIM is with your celebrant, or your CNI is on its way, the rest is the part you will remember.
journey.reaction: Warm without being eager. Good tone to end on.

unanswered_questions: Who in Dubai counts as an authorised witness, and can that appointment be arranged privately for us?
Can the small legal ceremony in Sydney be held privately, for example at a family home, and who has to be present beyond the two witnesses?
Who holds copies of our passports and birth certificates once they go to the celebrant, and how are they kept?
Have they planned a celebration abroad at 200 to 400 guests, with exclusive use and our own security working alongside the venue's?
Does one Wedded Advisor work alone, or is there a team behind them for an event of our size?
Is there a private or referral route to someone senior rather than the Wedded Concierge web page?

turn_offs_found.quote: One Wedded Advisor plans the venue, travel, vendors and payments with you as a single point of contact, anywhere in the world, and confirms the inclusions in writing before you commit.
turn_offs_found.why: 'Inclusions' is package language. It makes me picture a list of what comes in the bundle, which is exactly how I don't want to be treated. I want to hear what's possible, not what's included.

would_share_with: My assistant and family office, for the overseas witnessing rule, the timing window and the document list
My mother in Sydney, for the Option A section, since the legal ceremony would happen there

cta_reaction.quote: One Wedded Advisor plans the venue, travel, vendors and payments with you as a single point of contact, anywhere in the world, and confirms the inclusions in writing before you commit.
cta_reaction.why: 'Anywhere in the world' suits a family across Dubai, Sydney and London, and the tone is quiet. But it speaks to a standard couple: nothing on discretion or scale, and 'inclusions' sounds like a package. I wouldn't fill in a form. If someone we trust referred them, my assistant would make the call.

top_3_changes: In the closing 'Planning the celebration' paragraph, replace 'confirms the inclusions in writing' with wording about scope, such as 'confirms what is agreed in writing', so it doesn't read as package language.

In Option A, after 'You hold a small legal ceremony in Australia', add a question for the celebrant, such as where the legal ceremony can take place and who must be present, so a couple who wants a very private legal moment sees the point raised without the page making new claims.

In the Wedded Advisor paragraph, add one line inviting couples with large guest lists or privacy requirements to say so when they first get in touch, so scale and discretion are acknowledged without claiming capabilities the page can't support.

checks.check: Every journey point, turn-off and CTA reaction quotes the exact sentence from 05-draft.md
Stayed in character as Layla (UHNW, Dubai with family in Sydney; assistant reads first; cares about discretion, scale, being treated as more than a package client)
No invented brand facts; capability gaps listed as unanswered questions
Ignored HTML comments, image slots, CTA placeholders and VERIFY markers
Journey types limited to gained_trust, lost_trust, confused, bored, excited, objection; the one turn-off has a why
Deferred business details and transfers not treated as must-fix; absent prices, fees and translation detail accepted by design; no request for sourcing

assumptions: Layla's family plans a small legal ceremony in Sydney (Option A) and a large celebration abroad, with the couple living in Dubai when the NOIM is signed.
Her assistant read the page first and summarised, per decision_behaviour, within a 5-minute budget.
Guest count of about 300, within the card's 200 to 400.
